attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the cash-burn comparison in his own commentary.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm cash-burn ranking and the qualified description of coding's productivity potential. The latter does not hedge the financial assertion.

contract.note: Comparing aggregate net cash burn across applications is an ordinary reading. The latest completed quarter is a reasonable operational proxy, although Marcus supplied no period. That choice does not determine the result because comparable application-level figures are absent.

evidence.note: The filing was available before the cutoff and documents consolidated reporting. It supplies no comparable first-quarter cash burn by application and cannot establish the ranking.
This company disclosure covers February usage and was available before the cutoff. Coding activity and workflow changes do not measure net cash burn or establish its ranking.

reviews.rationale: Neither evidence item provides comparable cash flows for coding and other applications. Usage patterns and consolidated reporting establish neither the asserted ranking nor a counterexample. The packet therefore leaves the firm financial observation unresolved.
